Author: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
Bench: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
 Office Notes,
 reports, orders
Sl. or proceedings
 Date Court'S Or Judges'S Order

S No or directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  WPMS 1372/2024  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate, for the petitioners.
Mr. Suyash Pant, Brief Holder, for the State.
(2) According to petitioners, their land was acquired by National Highways Authority of India for expansion of National Highway No. 72.
The grievance raised by petitioners is regarding non- payment of compensation.

Petitioners submit that the amount determined by the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition has been deposited by the National Highways Authority of India with the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Dehradun, but the amount so deposited is not being released in their favour.

The relief sought in the writ petition is as follows:
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondent Special Land Acquisition Officer, Dehradun to release the compensation amount in favour of the petitioners in respect of the land bearing Khasra No. 540(Ga)
having an area of 0.384 hectares situated at Mauza Shishambada, Tehsil Vikas Nagar,
Dehradun inasmuch as the amount of compensation for the land acquired for has already been deposited by NHAI with the SLAO, Dehradun along with interest on the delay payment."
(3) Learned Counsel for the respondents has drawn attention of this Court to the order dated 15.3.2023, passed by Competent Authority/Special Land Acquisition Officer, Dehradun.
Perusal of the said order reveals that there is a dispute regarding title over the land, which was acquired by the National Highways Authority of India, and the said dispute has been referred for adjudication to Principal Civil Court under Section 3H(4) of National Highways Act, 1956.

Section 3H(4) of the said Act is reproduced below:-
WPMS/1372/2024 on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179829434/
1

"If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated."

(4) Since there is a dispute regarding ownership over the land, in question, therefore,
the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition was justified in referring the dispute to Principal Civil Court under Section 3H(4) of the aforesaid Act.

(5) Having regard to the facts of the case, writ petition is disposed of with a request to District Judge, Dehradun to make endeavour to decide the reference made under Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 as early as possible, preferably within four months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
(6) It shall be open to petitioners to raise all contentions before the Court concerned.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 3.6.2024 Pr WPMS/1372/2024 on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179829434/
2
